# Colecto v0.3.1

Proton Mail Bridge and other self-signed or STARTTLS-only mail servers can now be
added, and the Linux background services can be updated from the app.

## Mail accounts

- **IMAP STARTTLS:** the incoming server has a Security choice, TLS or STARTTLS
  (usually port 143). If a server refuses STARTTLS, Colecto disconnects before sending
  your password.
- **Any SMTP port:** the outgoing server takes any port. Port 465 uses TLS from the
  start, and every other port requires STARTTLS.
- **Trusted certificate:** an account can trust one specific certificate, such as the
  one Proton Mail Bridge exports, instead of your system's certificate authorities.
  Host names are still checked.
- **Proton Mail Bridge:** see the
  [setup steps](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.1/docs/accounts.md#proton-mail-bridge).
  This was tested against a stand-in server on Linux, not a real Bridge yet, and
  certificates issued to an IP address are untested on Windows and macOS.

## Background services on Linux

- The daemon and notifier services installed from Settings → Connection now record
  the Colecto version that wrote them. After you upgrade, Connection shows an
  **Update** button that rewrites the service and restarts it if it is running, so it
  stops running the old version. See
  [unit versions and updates](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.1/docs/self-hosting.md#unit-versions-and-updates).
  This has only been tested with a simulated systemd.

## Downloads and limits

Downloads are the same as in v0.3.0 and are still not code-signed; see
[installing](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.1/docs/install.md). The
[known limits](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.1/docs/roadmap.md)
still apply, and storage formats may change between alpha versions.
